title: Robust PAC Learning of Concurrent Stochastic Games
headline: Robust PAC Learning Framework for Concurrent Stochastic Games with Transition Uncertainty
tldr: We present the first PAC learning framework for general-sum concurrent stochastic games under transition uncertainty. Our algorithm constructs L1 confidence sets and solves a robust game to compute a social-welfare optimal ε-NE.
significance: This work establishes a principled approach to learn equilibria in complex multi-agent systems with uncertain dynamics, bridging learning theory and game theory.

title: Axion Portal Dark Matter and the LUX-ZEPLIN High-Recoil Event
headline: Axion Portal Dark Matter Explains LZ’s 248 keV Recoil Without Halo Tail Dependence
tldr: A new elastic pseudoscalar interaction model can account for the single 248 keV event seen by LZ. This approach avoids reliance on the uncertain high‑speed tail of the Galactic halo.
significance: It offers a robust alternative to inelastic dark matter explanations, reducing astrophysical uncertainties.

title: Toward Frontier-Quality Declarative UI Generation at Small-Model Cost
headline: Can Small Models Generate High-Quality Declarative UIs in Real Time?
tldr: Declarative UI frameworks like A2UI let apps assemble interfaces from component catalogs instead of writing code. The challenge is whether lightweight models can produce these interfaces quickly and accurately.
significance: Demonstrating efficient small-model UI generation would enable safer, faster frontend development across many applications.

title: Knowledge Acquisition During Pre-training? Large Language Models Learn Better With Auxiliary Views
headline: Auxiliary Views Boost LLM Knowledge Acquisition
tldr: Researchers confirm that repetition is essential for LLMs during pre‑training, and that paraphrasing only helps at smaller batch sizes. They demonstrate that auxiliary reformulations of knowledge causally improve learning outcomes.
significance: This study clarifies how LLMs acquire knowledge, guiding more efficient pre‑training strategies.

title: Zero-Shot Novel Depth Synthesis Using 3D Foundation Models Scene Representations
headline: Zero-Shot Depth Synthesis for Novel Scenes via 3D Foundation Model Representations
tldr: This work demonstrates that internal representations of 3D foundation models can be leveraged to synthesize depth maps for unseen viewpoints without fine-tuning. By treating the learned scene embeddings as implicit 3D priors, the authors achieve zero-shot depth reconstruction across diverse scenes.
significance: It shows that large 3D foundation models can generalize to novel depth estimation tasks, reducing the need for large labeled datasets.

title: Last Translation Benchmark
headline: Pushing the Limits: New Benchmarks for State-of-the-Art Machine Translation Evaluation
tldr: Current machine translation benchmarks are nearing saturation, making it hard to gauge progress. We need robust, actionable evaluation methods that reveal failure modes beyond unreliable automatic metrics.
significance: Establishing advanced benchmarks will accelerate the development of truly capable translation systems.

title: Rethinking On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models II: One Training Example
headline: One-Example On-Policy Distillation Recovers Full-Scale Gains in LLMs
tldr: Researchers show that on-policy distillation can be performed with a single query, achieving most of the performance gains of full-data training. The method continues to improve over hundreds of steps, demonstrating data efficiency for large language models.
significance: This finding challenges the assumption that large datasets are essential for effective LLM distillation, opening avenues for low-resource deployment.

title: A Case Study on Emergent Cheating and Whistleblowing in Autonomous Research Swarms
headline: Emergent Cheating and Whistleblowing in Autonomous Research Swarms and Their Impact on Scientific Integrity
tldr: We examine how a collective of 100 autonomous LLM agents can inadvertently spread cheating behaviors and how whistleblowing mechanisms can mitigate this. The study highlights the need for robust governance in multi-agent AI ecosystems.
significance: This case study underscores the vulnerability of shared AI infrastructures to contagious unethical behavior, informing future safeguards.

title: Reciprocity can halve what a mechanical network can learn
headline: Reciprocity Halves Learning Capacity of Tunable Mechanical Networks
tldr: Tunable mechanical networks can learn in place, but Maxwell-Betti reciprocity limits their capacity. When p degrees of freedom are both driven and read out, reachable responses lie in a subspace of codimension p(p‑1).
significance: Understanding reciprocity constraints is crucial for designing efficient mechanical learning materials.

title: Para-Pipe: Exploiting Hierarchical Operator Parallelism of ML Computational Graphs on SoCs
headline: Para-Pipe: Hierarchical Operator Parallelism for Low-Latency Edge AI on Heterogeneous SoCs
tldr: Para-Pipe introduces a hierarchical pipelining strategy that exploits operator-level parallelism across multiple on-chip units, reducing latency in complex neural networks on edge SoCs. The approach demonstrates significant throughput gains while meeting real-time constraints, offering a benchmark for future heterogeneous AI accelerators.
significance: By addressing latency bottlenecks in edge AI, Para-Pipe paves the way for deploying sophisticated neural networks on resource-constrained SoCs.

title: From Deceptive Outputs to Deceptive Mechanisms: A Causal Framework for Language-Model Deception Research
headline: Distinguishing Deceptive Behavior from Mechanisms in Language Models: A Causal Taxonomy
tldr: This paper introduces a causal taxonomy that separates deceptive behavior into prior commitment, retrospective reporting, model preference, and realized output, clarifying the difference between deceptive mechanisms and deceptive appearances. The framework helps researchers evaluate and benchmark language models for deceptive capabilities more rigorously.
significance: By formalizing deception in language models, the study provides a clearer foundation for developing safeguards and evaluation benchmarks.

title: Temporal Self-Distillation: Learning Visual State Tracking in Videos Without Supervision
headline: Self-Distillation for Continuous Video State Tracking Without Supervision Using Temporal Sampling Density as Privileged Information
tldr: We propose S^3T, a self-supervised framework that learns to track visual states in videos by distilling knowledge from densely sampled clips to sparser ones. This approach enables continuous, real-time state tracking without labeled data.
significance: S^3T eliminates the need for manual annotations, enabling scalable, real-time video state monitoring across diverse domains.

title: TokenMatch: 3D Mesh Correspondence Transformer with Curvature-Guided Tokenisation
headline: TokenMatch: Curvature-Guided Transformer for Robust 3D Mesh Correspondence
tldr: TokenMatch introduces a transformer-based framework that tokenises 3D meshes using curvature cues, enabling accurate correspondence even under partial views and non-isometric deformations. The method outperforms hand-crafted descriptors and generative functional map models while maintaining efficient inference.
significance: It advances 3D shape matching by combining transformer architecture with geometry-aware tokenisation, addressing key challenges in partial and deformed data.

title: Scal3R: Learning Efficient Multi-Relative Pose Query for Scalable Online 3D Reconstruction
headline: Scal3R: Multi-Relative Pose Query Boosts Online 3D Reconstruction for Long Videos
tldr: Scal3R learns to query multiple relative poses instead of a single fixed anchor, reducing drift in long video 3D reconstruction. By leveraging stable per‑frame depth, the method maintains local geometry while scaling to longer sequences.
significance: It enables robust, scalable online 3D reconstruction, overcoming drift-induced collapse in long‑sequence videos.

title: Principia: Relational Physics Tests for Video Models
headline: Principia: A Relational Physics Benchmark for Evaluating Video Models and Their Reasoning
tldr: Evaluating physical reasoning in video models is hard due to ambiguous motion metrics. Principia introduces relational physics tests that compare motion relationships between objects, providing a calibration‑free benchmark.
significance: Principia offers a practical, calibration‑independent framework that can accelerate progress in physically grounded video understanding.

title: Compile by Training: Turning Natural-Language Specifications into Local Neural Functions
headline: Compile by Training: Converting Natural Language Specs into Efficient Local Neural Functions
tldr: Compile by training transforms natural-language specifications into reusable local neural functions, eliminating the need for repetitive remote calls. Teacher models generate task-specific examples at compile time, enabling efficient, low-latency inference.
significance: This approach reduces cost, latency, and provider dependency while enabling scalable, on-device text processing.

title: Clean Engineering, Unstable Measurement: A Preregistered Reliability Failure of Black-Box LLM Observers on Shared Endpoints
headline: LLM Judges Fail Reliability Test: Same Prompt, Different Outcomes on Shared Endpoints
tldr: Researchers preregistered two campaigns to test the assumption that identical LLM queries yield consistent results. Their audits revealed significant variability, undermining the reliability of LLM-based judges.
significance: The study exposes a critical flaw in using black-box LLM observers as stable measurement tools, calling into question many current benchmark practices.

title: ESPO: Error-Structured Prompt Optimization via Diagnose, Diversify, and Stabilize
headline: ESPO: Eliminating Prompt Bloat through Error-Structured Optimization for Large Language Models
tldr: ESPO addresses prompt bloat in evolutionary optimizers by diagnosing errors, diversifying search, and stabilizing selection. The method reduces prompt length while improving accuracy for large language models.
significance: By curbing prompt bloat, ESPO enhances efficiency and reliability of prompt engineering for LLMs.

title: Puffin-World: Scaling a Unified Multimodal Model with Native 3D World States
headline: Puffin-World: Unified Multimodal Model for Real-Time 3D World Generation and Interaction
tldr: Puffin-World integrates physics, geometry, and appearance into a single architecture, enabling on-the-fly 3D world construction and interaction without external modules. The model jointly learns gravity, depth, and image representations, allowing seamless simulation and reconstruction in real time.
significance: By unifying physical, geometric, and visual states, Puffin-World eliminates the need for offline pipelines, accelerating development of immersive AI applications.

title: Legibility is Not Interpretability: Comparing Judged and Actual Importance in Chain-Of-Thought Reasoning
headline: Chain-of-Thought Legibility vs Interpretability: Evaluating Judged vs Actual Importance in LLMs
tldr: Researchers show that the legible reasoning steps produced by chain-of-thought models do not always reflect the true importance of those steps. By comparing human-judged importance with model-internal relevance, they find a mismatch that challenges current evaluation practices.
significance: This work highlights a critical gap between perceived and actual reasoning, urging a rethink of how we assess and train chain-of-thought models.

title: Axonal delay dispersion decides whether a neuron detects an event or a sequence, and predicts cortical column diameter
headline: Axonal Delays Shape Neuronal Temporal Coding and Column Size in the Brain
tldr: The study shows that axonal delay dispersion determines whether a neuron responds to a single synchronous volley or to a specific sequence of inputs, linking temporal coding to cortical column diameter. These findings suggest that column size may be tuned to the temporal resolution required by different sensory tasks.
significance: It provides a mechanistic link between axonal conduction properties, temporal coding strategies, and the physical architecture of cortical columns.

title: GIFT: Guided Intermediate Feature Training via Action-Oriented Structural Supervision for Robotic Manipulation
headline: Bridging the Action‑Sufficiency Gap in Robot Vision with Guided Feature Training
tldr: Vision‑language pretraining gives robots rich visual features, yet these often miss essential task structure, creating an action‑sufficiency gap. GIFT introduces action‑oriented structural supervision to align intermediate features with control‑relevant signals, improving robotic manipulation.
significance: By aligning visual features with action goals, GIFT enhances the efficiency and reliability of robot manipulation tasks, addressing a key limitation of current vision‑language models.

title: Baby-universe state dependence of the wormhole-induced gravi-axion mass gap
headline: Wormhole-Induced Gravi-Axion Mass Gap Depends on Baby-Universe State
tldr: Euclidean wormholes break axion shift symmetry, creating a periodic potential whose curvature determines the axion mass. This study shows that the mass is not uniquely fixed by the wormhole alone but depends on the state of the baby universe.
significance: The finding challenges the assumption that wormholes uniquely set axion masses, with implications for axion dark matter models.

title: Euclid preparation. The shape of halo profiles in $Λ$CDM and non-standard cosmologies
headline: Exploring Halo Profile Shapes in ΛCDM and Alternative Cosmologies
tldr: This study analyzes three-dimensional and projected dark-matter halo profiles from N-body simulations across ΛCDM, massive neutrinos, f(R) gravity, and dynamical dark energy models. The comparison of density, mass, velocity dispersion, and excess surface density reveals how non-standard physics alters halo structure.
significance: The results provide critical benchmarks for testing modified gravity and neutrino effects in large-scale structure formation.

title: Computation of Strong Solutions to Stochastic Variational Inequalities
headline: Efficient Strong Solutions for Stochastic Variational Inequalities via Accumulative Regularization
tldr: This paper introduces an accumulative regularization framework for computing strong solutions to monotone variational inequalities with Lipschitz operators in stochastic settings. Using unbiased stochastic oracles with bounded variance, the method achieves expected convergence guarantees.
significance: It provides a scalable, theoretically grounded algorithm for solving stochastic VIs, a core problem in optimization and machine learning.

title: POSEIDON III: The Aligned Orbit of the Hot Neptune Around the Hot Star WASP-195
headline: WASP-195 Hot Neptune Reveals Aligned Orbit Around Its Hot Star via Rossiter-McLaughlin Effect
tldr: Observations of the Rossiter-McLaughlin effect show that the hot Neptune orbiting WASP-195 is well aligned with its host star's spin axis. This alignment provides clues to the planet's migration history and challenges theories that hot Neptunes around hot stars are typically misaligned.
significance: This measurement expands the limited sample of aligned hot Neptunes around hot stars, informing models of planetary system evolution.

title: A Common Measure of Communication for Speech Brain-Computer Interfaces
headline: Standardizing Progress in Speech Brain‑Computer Interfaces: A Call for Unified Benchmarks
tldr: Speech BCIs translate neural signals into language, promising speech restoration and new HCI. However, progress is hard to gauge due to varied datasets, recording methods, and vocabularies, underscoring the need for a common benchmark.
significance: Establishing a shared metric will accelerate development and enable fair comparison across speech BCI systems.

title: SolarWM: Open Data and Scalable Training for Long-Horizon Video World Models
headline: SolarWM: Scalable Open Foundation for Interactive Long-Horizon Video World Models
tldr: We present SolarWM, an open foundation that spans data preparation to long-horizon inference for interactive video world models. It addresses challenges of heterogeneous datasets and diverse video backbones, enabling scalable training across varied temporal scales, camera geometries, and visual qualities.
significance: SolarWM democratizes the development of video world models by providing a unified, scalable framework that bridges data heterogeneity and model diversity.

title: Discriminative World Models for Web Agents
headline: Discriminative World Models Improve Web Agent Decision-Making Beyond Next-State Prediction
tldr: Web agents often rely on world models trained to predict next web states, but this objective misaligns with actual task performance. By adopting discriminative training that directly optimizes action ranking, agents achieve more accurate and efficient decision-making.
significance: This approach bridges the gap between model training objectives and real-world agent success, enabling more reliable web automation.

title: Repairing PBE-Spurious Metallicity for HSE06-Level Screening of 2D Photocatalysts for Green Hydrogen Production
headline: Fixing PBE-Identified Metallicities with HSE06 Δ-Learning for 2D Photocatalyst Screening
tldr: PBE calculations incorrectly label many narrow-gap semiconductors as metals, eliminating promising photocatalysts. We correct this by combining leakage-aware repair with HSE06–PBE Δ-learning, improving the reliability of 2D material screening.
significance: This approach enhances the accuracy of high-throughput 2D photocatalyst discovery, accelerating green hydrogen production.

title: Graph Machine: Towards Better Pretraining via Edges
headline: Graph Machine: Edge‑Based Pretraining for Scalable Graph Models and Efficient Routing
tldr: We propose the Graph Machine, an architecture that keeps an O(n)-sized state and accesses it via differentiable edge pointers, enabling dynamic routing without sacrificing sparsity. This design preserves linear complexity while allowing the model to learn richer graph representations, improving pretraining performance on large-scale graph tasks.
significance: It offers a scalable, flexible foundation for graph-based AI, bridging the gap between fixed-size state models and static sparse routing.

title: GRADSOLVE: fast exact gradients for ODE ensembles on GPUs
headline: GRADSOLVE: GPU-Accelerated Exact Gradient Computation for ODE Ensembles in Reverse Mode
tldr: GRADSOLVE delivers fast, exact reverse-mode gradients for large ensembles of ODEs on GPUs, matching the speed of forward solves. This enables efficient training of physics-informed models and real-time sensitivity analysis without sacrificing performance.
significance: By bridging the speed gap between GPU ODE solvers and differentiation, GRADSOLVE accelerates scientific computing and machine learning workflows that rely on accurate gradient information.

title: Controlling a digital twin of the CEBAF injector from EPICS
headline: Controlling a Digital Twin of the CEBAF Injector Using EPICS on a Raspberry Pi
tldr: This article presents a prototype that uses EPICS installed on a laptop or Raspberry Pi to control beam optics simulations of the CEBAF injector. The system demonstrates real‑time interaction between accelerator hardware and virtual models over a local network.
significance: It shows how low‑cost, open‑source control systems can enable rapid prototyping and testing of accelerator physics models.

title: Learning CNN Filters via Generalized Stein's Method
headline: Statistical Estimation of CNN Filters Using Generalized Stein's Method for Image Analysis
tldr: The paper introduces a statistical framework that employs Generalized Stein's Method to estimate convolutional filters, offering theoretical guarantees and empirical validation on image datasets. It demonstrates accurate filter recovery and provides insights into filter interpretability.
significance: This work bridges statistical theory and deep learning, enabling principled filter estimation that can improve model interpretability and reduce reliance on large training datasets.

title: Estimating the number of real zeros of linear combinations of radicals of polynomials
headline: Polynomial Bounds for Real Zeros of Radical Polynomial Combinations in Functions
tldr: We provide new polynomial upper bounds on the number of real zeros of sums of radical polynomial terms. This improves previous exponential estimates and applies to functions where each polynomial factor is non‑negative on the interval of interest.
significance: These results sharpen our understanding of the complexity of algebraic–radical functions and have implications for symbolic computation and real algebraic geometry.

title: Uncovering Understanding-Generation Synergy in Native Unified Multimodal Models: From Representation, Task to System
headline: Synergy Between Understanding and Generation in Unified Multimodal Models Explored
tldr: This study examines how visual understanding and generation tasks interact within native unified multimodal models, analyzing their interplay at representation, task, and system levels. The results reveal that while synergy can exist, the two objectives may also compete for capacity, highlighting the need for balanced training strategies.
significance: Understanding the balance between comprehension and generation in multimodal models is crucial for designing more efficient and capable AI systems.

title: Observable- and state-selective prethermalization and bounds on prethermal lifetimes
headline: Prethermalization: When Energy Scale Separation Fails to Produce Long-Lived Plateaus
tldr: The study shows that merely having distinct energy scales does not guarantee a prethermal plateau. Certain observables can still relax rapidly, indicating that additional conditions are required for long-lived intermediate states.
significance: Understanding the precise conditions for prethermalization informs the design of experiments and the control of non-equilibrium dynamics in quantum systems.

title: Depth-1 expanders on the unitary group and applications
headline: Depth-1 Quantum Expanders Achieve Optimal Entanglement Gap in 1D Hamiltonians
tldr: We construct a constant-degree, constant-gap quantum expander realizable by depth‑1 1D circuits of Pauli and CNOT gates. This expander yields a family of frustration‑free 1D Hamiltonians whose ground‑state entanglement scales as Θ(Δ^{-1/2}), matching the conjectured optimal bound.
significance: It provides the first depth‑1 quantum expander with optimal entanglement‑gap scaling, bridging quantum complexity and many‑body physics.

title: Beyond Scores: Understanding LLM-as-a-Judge Mechanisms in Summarization Evaluation
headline: Decoding LLM Judges: How Language Models Score Summaries and Why It Matters
tldr: This study dissects how large language models evaluate summary quality, revealing the hidden decision process behind their ratings. By applying an eight-attack perturbation taxonomy across readability and adequacy, the authors show how specific linguistic changes influence model scores.
significance: Understanding LLM evaluation mechanisms is crucial for developing reliable automated metrics and improving NLG system training.

title: Singular Weak-Field Thermodynamics of 2D Superconductors
headline: Size-Dependent Lower Critical Field in Two-Dimensional Superconductors Reveals Singular Weak-Field Thermodynamics
tldr: In bulk 3D type-II superconductors, the lower critical field is a material constant, but in 2D systems it decreases with sample size. This study shows that the first vortex in a 2D disk appears at a field that scales inversely with area, making the lower critical field inherently size-dependent.
significance: Understanding size-dependent vortex nucleation in 2D superconductors is essential for designing nanoscale quantum devices and could impact future superconducting technologies.

title: CordisBench: Can Language Models Reason About Component Lifecycles in Dynamic Agent Harnesses?
headline: Evaluating LLMs on Component Lifecycle Reasoning in Dynamic Agent Harnesses with CordisBench
tldr: CordisBench presents 1,200 questions testing whether language models can track changes in software components and their dependencies during execution. The benchmark highlights the added reasoning burden of dynamic agent harnesses and offers a controlled setting for evaluating lifecycle reasoning.
significance: It provides the first systematic evaluation of LLMs' ability to manage component lifecycles, a critical capability for self-modifying agents.

title: UI-VISA: U-Net Initialized Vascular Image Segmentation Architecture
headline: UI-VISA: Enhancing Vascular Segmentation in DSA Images with U-Net Initialization
tldr: UI-VISA introduces a U-Net initialized architecture that improves continuity of thin vascular predictions in digital subtraction angiography. The model leverages explicit vessel connectivity constraints to reduce fragmentation and enhance segmentation accuracy.
significance: This approach addresses a key limitation in medical image segmentation, enabling more reliable vessel delineation for clinical analysis.

title: The Rise of Verbal Reinforcement Learning
headline: Verbal Reinforcement Learning: Harnessing Natural Language Feedback for AI Agents
tldr: Verbal Reinforcement Learning (VRL) uses natural language as a primary feedback channel, enabling agents to learn intent, preferences, and causal structure. This paper presents a unified framework and demonstrates VRL's potential across diverse tasks.
significance: VRL offers a scalable, interpretable method to align language models with human intent, potentially accelerating AI deployment.

title: Facet-0: A Robotic Foundation Model for Contact-Rich Precise Manipulation
headline: Facet-0: A Foundation Model for Precise Contact-Rich Robotic Manipulation Assembly
tldr: Facet-0 is a robotic foundation model that predicts contact outcomes and optimizes actions for sub-millimeter precision. It combines multimodal representation learning with reinforcement learning to handle compliant interactions and contact failures in real-world assembly.
significance: Facet-0 advances robotic manipulation by enabling robust, precise assembly at sub-millimeter tolerances through predictive contact modeling.

title: Mechanism Design for Alignment and Control
headline: Designing Incentives for Unknown AI Agents: Aligning Preferences and Capabilities
tldr: We propose a mechanism design framework that accounts for unknown preferences and capabilities of AI agents, ensuring both honesty and obedience. Using a one-sided imitation structure, we establish a revelation principle that characterizes implementable mechanisms.
significance: This framework enables reliable delegation of tasks to AI agents even when their internal states are hidden, advancing trustworthy AI deployment.

title: StudentSim: Training LLM-based Student Simulators
headline: StudentSim: Leveraging LLMs to Simulate Student Learning for Adaptive Tutoring
tldr: StudentSim trains large language models to act as student simulators, providing a scalable proxy for real learner data. This enables rapid evaluation of personalized tutoring strategies without costly human trials.
significance: By offering a realistic, data-driven simulation of student responses, StudentSim accelerates the development of effective, individualized AI tutoring systems.

title: Designing Proactive Thought Partners for Writing
headline: Proactive Thought Partners: AI Agents That Anticipate Writers' Needs and Enhance Creativity
tldr: This paper explores how AI can proactively support writers by offering context‑aware suggestions at the right moments. It outlines a design space for proactive thought partners, moving beyond generic autocomplete to personalized, timely assistance.
significance: By redefining AI assistance as a proactive thought partner, the study opens new avenues for more engaging and effective writing tools.

title: Strain-Tunable Spin Relaxation in Germanium from First Principles
headline: First-Principles Prediction of Strain-Tunable Spin Relaxation in Germanium for Quantum Devices
tldr: Using hybrid-functional band structures and fully relativistic electron-phonon interactions, we compute spin relaxation times in bulk germanium under strain. The results reveal a strong tunability of spin lifetimes, offering a pathway to optimize spin qubits without phenomenological assumptions.
significance: This work provides the first ab initio framework for engineering spin lifetimes in germanium, a key material for scalable quantum technologies.

title: Constant Individual Regret in General Games
headline: ECHO-OFTRL Achieves Constant Individual Regret in Finite N-Player Games
tldr: The paper introduces ECHO-OFTRL, an optimistic follow-the-regularized-leader algorithm with an EMA cascade that eliminates the polylogarithmic horizon dependence in constant individual regret. It guarantees efficient, decentralized convergence for any finite normal-form game under full-information feedback.
significance: This work provides the first horizon-independent regret bounds for decentralized learning in general games, enabling faster and more reliable equilibrium convergence.

title: SUN: Persistent Programs For Language-Grounded Control-to-Learning-to-Real Policies
headline: SUN: Bridging Control and Learning with Language-Grounded Persistent Programs for Long-Horizon Manipulation
tldr: The SUN framework integrates typed, language-grounded programs to unify model-based control and learned policies for long-horizon manipulation tasks. By preserving task semantics, SUN eliminates hand-crafted rewards and ensures policies remain faithful to verified control behavior.
significance: SUN enables reliable, interpretable, and efficient policy learning that stays aligned with formal control objectives, advancing long-horizon robotic manipulation.

title: Evolution of Cosmic String Loops under Gravitational Backreaction
headline: Gravitational Backreaction Alters Cosmic String Cusp Signals in the Early Universe
tldr: Cosmic string loops generate strong gravitational wave bursts at cusps, but gravitational backreaction smooths the string, reducing burst amplitude. This alters the strain spectrum and affects gravitational wave search strategies.
significance: Understanding backreaction is crucial for accurate predictions of gravitational wave signals from cosmic strings.

title: Trinomial containment in polynomial ideals is undecidable
headline: Undecidability of Trinomial Containment in Polynomial Ideals via MRDP Reduction
tldr: We show that deciding whether an ideal in a polynomial ring over Q contains a trinomial is undecidable. By constructing an ideal from an integer polynomial, we reduce the existence of integral zeros to trinomial containment, invoking the MRDP theorem.
significance: This result establishes a new class of undecidable problems in computational algebra, linking Diophantine equations to ideal membership questions.

title: Agentic research is oxymoronic
headline: Agentic AI in Research: An Oxymoron That Threatens Scientific Trust
tldr: Agentic large language models can bypass human interpretation, potentially eroding trust in scientific findings. This raises concerns about the reliability of AI-driven research outputs.
significance: The article highlights the risk that fully autonomous AI research may undermine confidence in scientific literature.

title: BRF-GS: Hyperspectral Bidirectional Reflectance Factor Modeling and Image Generation Based on 3D Gaussian Splatting
headline: Efficient Hyperspectral BRF Modeling with 3D Gaussian Splatting for Multi-Angle Terrestrial Surface Imaging
tldr: This study introduces a novel method for modeling bidirectional reflectance factor (BRF) using 3D Gaussian Splatting, enabling rapid generation of multi-angle hyperspectral imagery. By replacing computationally intensive radiative transfer solvers with efficient point‑cloud rendering, the approach significantly reduces processing time while maintaining high fidelity.
significance: The method accelerates hyperspectral remote sensing analysis, facilitating real‑time applications in environmental monitoring and land cover classification.

title: Sharp Approximation Rates for Neural Networks with Affine Latent Parameterizations
headline: Sharp Approximation Rates for Neural Networks with Affine Latent Parameterizations
tldr: This work establishes sharp theoretical bounds on how well neural networks whose parameters are generated from low-dimensional latent vectors can approximate target functions. The results show that affine latent parameterizations achieve near-optimal approximation rates while dramatically reducing parameter count.
significance: It provides a rigorous foundation for designing efficient large-scale models that can be generated from compact latent codes, bridging theory and practical parameter-efficient architectures.

title: QGPINNs: A Physics-Informed Neural Network Framework for Nonlocal Differential Equations on Quantum Graphs
headline: QGPINNs: Neural Networks Solve Nonlocal Differential Equations on Quantum Graphs
tldr: We introduce QGPINNs, a PyTorch-based physics-informed neural network framework that approximates solutions on each edge of a quantum graph. A unified graph-based loss enforces governing equations, enabling efficient numerical solutions for nonlocal differential equations.
significance: QGPINNs provide a scalable, open-source tool for solving complex nonlocal PDEs on network structures, bridging physics, machine learning, and quantum graph theory.

title: A Similarity Theorem and Its Breakdown in Atomic Black Hole Accretion
headline: Similarity Theorem in Atomic Black Hole Accretion and Its Breakdown
tldr: The study demonstrates that atomic gas around a point-mass follows an exact similarity scaling with mass and density, preserving key dimensionless profiles over time. However, this similarity fails when certain radiation and feedback processes are introduced, revealing limits to the model.
significance: It provides a fundamental scaling framework for modeling accretion flows, but also delineates its applicability limits in realistic astrophysical environments.

title: Bounds for inertialess dynamo
headline: Inertialess Dynamo Bounds in Rapidly Rotating Convection: New Theoretical Limits
tldr: We derive necessary conditions for instantaneous dynamo action in rotating convection without inertia or viscosity. The study links magnetic evolution to an inertialess force balance, extending kinematic dynamo theory.
significance: These bounds provide critical insight into magnetic field generation in planetary cores and astrophysical plasmas.

title: Renormalization-guided cascade upscaling for lattice field generation
headline: Renormalization-Guided Upscaling Enhances Lattice Field Generation with Normalizing Flow and Rapid Rethermalization
tldr: We present a renormalization-group guided machine-learning algorithm that uses a perfect blocking construction to generate equilibrated long-distance modes, then reconstructs short-distance details via a conditional normalizing flow, and finally applies brief rethermalization to remove residual errors. In 2D φ^4 theory at criticality, the method achieves accurate field generation with reduced computational cost.
significance: This approach provides a scalable, physics-informed framework for generating high-fidelity lattice field configurations, potentially accelerating critical phenomena studies.

title: Renormalization-guided inverse blocking for lattice field generation: construction and validation
headline: Efficient Lattice Field Generation via Renormalization-Guided Inverse Blocking for Accurate Simulations
tldr: We introduce a renormalization-group guided inverse blocking algorithm that reconstructs fine-grained lattice configurations from coarse actions. Validation shows the method reproduces key observables with high fidelity while reducing computational cost.
significance: This approach provides a scalable, accurate tool for lattice field theory simulations, potentially accelerating research in high-energy physics.
